data.and-the-shared-reader-is-where-the-next-:
Reading a real Kindle book is also what found go-richdoc/html#4: a space following an inline element is dropped, so Walt Whitman has comes out as one word. It had been there all along, under epub and email too — any paragraph with an , a , a or a link loses a space at every one of those boundaries.
What made it visible was a second rendering of the same text: Project Gutenberg publishes a MOBI and a plain text of every title it has, and 125 816 words against 126 630 is a question a reader cannot ask of its own output. A shared reader multiplies a defect by its callers, which is the same property that made it worth writing once.
A one-line summary each, and nothing more: what a converter does with a construct its format cannot express lives in that repository’s README, beside the measurement that decided it, so there is one place to correct when it changes.
data.modules#Modules:
The 10 modules of go-richdoc. Each links to its source and to its generated API reference.
Module What it is Directions Reference richdoc the model itself: the tree, and Walk, Clone, PlainText and a builder — pkg.go.dev markdown CommonMark + GFM tables and strikethrough, delegating the parse to goldmark read, write pkg.go.dev latex a practical subset of LaTeX, plus a PDF subpackage read, write pkg.go.dev rst reStructuredText, delegating the parse to go-docutils/docutils read, write pkg.go.dev data CSV, JSON, XML and plain text, plus the richdata command — cobra with POSIX flags since v0.3.0 (--format, not -format), exiting 2 for a bad command line and 1 for work that failed read pkg.go.dev fb2 FictionBook 2 (.fb2): one XML file, images base64 inside it read pkg.go.dev html HTML and XHTML, delegating the parse to golang.org/x/net/html read pkg.go.dev epub EPUB 2 and 3: the ZIP, the manifest and the spine, chapters through html read pkg.go.dev email RFC 5322 messages and MIME, HTML parts through html read pkg.go.dev mobi Kindle MOBI: a Palm database, a PalmDOC stream and one HTML document, through html read pkg.go.dev Which directions a module has is in the table, because “converter” said of a one-way reader is the kind of claim that costs somebody an afternoon. A module that only reads is not unfinished: a .fb2, an EPUB, a mailbox or a .csv is a source, and writing one back is a job nobody has asked for.
data.one-missing-reader-was-three-missing-for: html is not a format anybody asked this organisation for. It is the piece epub and email both needed — EPUB’s content documents are XHTML and an HTML mail’s body is HTML — and mobi needed it as well: a MOBI’s text IS one HTML document, cut into 4096-byte pieces and each piece compressed on its own. Three entries on go-pdfkit’s parity table were blocked on one reader, which is the argument for naming a gap rather than working around it: all three are closed now, and the third is mobi.
